title: Sources and Schools of Personal Laws

content.overview: Indian family law is not a single code. Hindus (including Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs under the Hindu Code Acts), Muslims, Christians, Parsis and parties under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 are governed by different statutes and residual uncodified rules. Always identify which personal law applies before applying any section.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Which personal law? (2) Codified statute or residual classical rule? (3) Mitakshara or Dayabhaga if Hindu joint family? (4) SMA if civil/inter-religious?
content.study:
Hindu sources: Shruti, Smriti, commentaries (Mitakshara, Dayabhaga), custom, legislation, precedent. After codification, the Hindu Code Acts occupy much of the field; custom survives where saved.

Mitakshara: birthright coparcenary (modified by HSA 2005). Dayabhaga: Bengal school; no Mitakshara-type birthright.

Muslim sources: Quran, Sunnah, Ijma, Qiyas; schools. Statutes: Shariat Act 1937; DMMA 1939; Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

SMA 1954: secular civil marriage for any two persons.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Identify personal law first
sections.body: Community and chosen statute determine the applicable rules.

sections.heading: Hindu sources and schools
sections.body: Traditional sources + Mitakshara/Dayabhaga; modern Code Acts.

sections.heading: Muslim sources and statutes
sections.body: Classical sources + Shariat Act and special statutes.

sections.heading: SMA as secular option
sections.body: Any two persons; civil notice and solemnisation.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Name personal law → statute → residual classical rule if any.

examples.title: Choosing the statute
examples.body: Two Hindus with saptapadi — HMA. Hindu and Christian before Marriage Officer — SMA. Muslim wife seeking judicial divorce — DMMA.

hypotheticals.question: Which law for an inter-religious civil marriage?
hypotheticals.analysis: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — not HMA unless both are Hindus as defined.

misconceptions.trap: Family law is one uniform code for all Indians.
misconceptions.correction: Personal laws differ by community; SMA is the main secular civil option.
